quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so other drivers will let you through.
Drive around a car if it is blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of at least:
questions.explanation: Drivers 21 or older cannot drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 percent or more. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: You cannot cross a single broken white or yellow line when:

options.text: It would interfere with other traffic.
You are turning left into a driveway.
The car ahead of you has broken down.
You are passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: It would interfere with other traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely and without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: Cars are passing you on both sides while you drive in the center lane of an expressway. What should you do?
questions.explanation: On roads with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. On interstate highways, use the right lane if you are driving slower than the traffic around you.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control how traffic moves. They are usually white with black markings. Drivers must always obey them.

questions.question: You should increase the distance between your car and the car ahead when:

options.text: You are following a small passenger car.
You are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: When being tailgated, add extra space in front of your car. Do not brake suddenly. Slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid a collision with the tailgater.

questions.question: When driving to a new area, you should:

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you leave.
Only have a general idea of where you are going.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you leave.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip in advance when driving to an unfamiliar area. Do not start with only a general idea of where you are going. Check the location on a map before you drive.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left. It is unsafe and against the law to turn left where this sign is posted.

questions.question: When you see a steady green arrow on a traffic signal, you:

options.text: Should move into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Should slow down and stop, if safe.
Can turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection go first.
Can drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection go first.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane. Always let vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection pass first.

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as cars to your right and left, you should:

options.text: Let the car on your left go first.
Let the car on your right go first.
Wait until there are no cars before you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car on your right go first.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or signals, the car on your right has the right-of-way. Other cars then go in the order they arrived.

questions.question: If a traffic light shows both red and a green arrow, can you turn in the direction of the arrow?
questions.explanation: You can turn in the direction of a green arrow after you yield to other traffic in the intersection or crosswalk. Other lights do not stop you from turning on a green arrow.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: Only if it is following you.
Only if it is approaching you from the opposite direction.

questions.explanation: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights. This applies whether the vehicle is behind you or coming toward you.

questions.question: In bad weather, what should you do?
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid sudden braking and sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Put one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car in front of you while driving.
Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for potential dangers. Staring only at the road directly in front of you is unsafe. Scan ahead and stay alert to vehicles around you.

questions.question: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.
Reduce your speed, move as far to the right as possible, and stop off the roadway.
Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed, move as far to the right as possible, and stop off the roadway.
questions.explanation: Slow down right away when you see heavy smoke ahead. Drive as far as you can to the right and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Heavy smoke can hurt your eyes and lungs or be dangerous in other ways.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When passing another car, when should you move back into the right lane?

options.text: You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.
You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you have enough space before moving back into the driving lane. When you can see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to the driving lane.

questions.question: In normal weather and traffic, what is the minimum following distance?
questions.explanation: Keep at least three seconds of distance between your vehicle and the car ahead under normal conditions. This gives you time to react. Increase this distance when weather or traffic conditions are poor.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mark school zones. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians when driving near a school.

questions.question: When visibility is reduced, what should you do first?

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.explanation: Your first action when you cannot see well should be to slow down. This helps you respond to dangerous road conditions.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are to your left, and parked vehicles are to your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Down the middle, between both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle, between both sides.
questions.explanation: When oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right, steer down the middle. This keeps you away from both hazards.

questions.question: When changing lanes, which action should you never do?

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes or pass in an intersection. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and watch for drivers entering the same lane.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into a driveway, enter or exit a highway, or make a legal U-turn.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. Your car should end up in which lane?

options.text: The lane with the least traffic.

questions.explanation: When you turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, complete your turn into the left lane. This is the lane closest to the lane you just left.

questions.question: In fog or mist, why should you not use high beam headlights?

options.text: The light reflects back into your eyes.
Vehicles behind you will follow too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light reflects back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights reflect back at you, making it harder to see. Use low beams instead.

questions.question: Your gas pedal sticks open while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If your gas pedal sticks, turn off the ignition carefully—only far enough to stop the engine, not lock the wheel. Then apply your brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: A vehicle ahead uses high beams toward you. Where should you look?

options.text: To either side of the road.
To the center of the road.
To the right side of the road.
To the left side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look to the right side of the road when oncoming high beams blind you. This prevents eye strain and helps you stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: Your car has no Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS). To stop quickly, you should:
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop quickly in an emergency. It stops your car fast and lets you keep steering.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Use both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head to look over your shoulder to check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection. It is unsafe and illegal to do so.
